accepted.question_text: For elliptic curves defined by cubic equations in two variables, does the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture hold: is the number of points on an elliptic curve modulo p related in the conjectured way to the rank of the group of rational points?

evidence.page: Unsolved problems > Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
evidence.quote: Supported by much experimental evidence, this conjecture relates the number of points on an elliptic curve mod p to the rank of the group of rational points.

evidence.page: Unsolved problems > Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
evidence.quote: Elliptic curves, defined by cubic equations in two variables, are fundamental mathematical objects that arise in many areas: Wiles’ proof of the Fermat Conjecture, factorization of numbers into primes, and cryptography, to name three.

accepted.question_text: For the solution set of a system of algebraic equations, how much of its topology can be defined in terms of further algebraic equations? The Clay Mathematics Institute page states that the Hodge conjecture is known in certain special cases, such as when the solution set has dimension less than four, but remains unknown in dimension four.

evidence.quote: The answer to this conjecture determines how much of the topology of the solution set of a system of algebraic equations can be defined in terms of further algebraic equations.
The Hodge conjecture is known in certain special cases, e.g., when the solution set has dimension less than four. But in dimension four it is unknown.

accepted.question_text: For the Navier-Stokes equation that governs the flow of fluids such as water and air, do solutions exist, and are they unique?

evidence.quote: This is the equation which governs the flow of fluids such as water and air. However, there is no proof for the most basic questions one can ask: do solutions exist, and are they unique?

accepted.question_text: If it is easy to check that a solution to a problem is correct, is it also easy to solve the problem?

evidence.quote: If it is easy to check that a solution to a problem is correct, is it also easy to solve the problem? This is the essence of the P vs NP question.

accepted.question_text: Are all the ‘non-obvious’ zeros of the zeta function complex numbers with real part 1/2?

evidence.quote: The Riemann hypothesis tells us about the deviation from the average. Formulated in Riemann’s 1859 paper, it asserts that all the ‘non-obvious’ zeros of the zeta function are complex numbers with real part 1/2.

accepted.question_text: Do the quantum versions of the Yang-Mills equations have a mass gap, as suggested by experiment and computer simulations?

evidence.page: Unsolved problems > Yang-Mills & the Mass Gap
evidence.quote: Experiment and computer simulations suggest the existence of a “mass gap” in the solution to the quantum versions of the Yang-Mills equations. But no proof of this property is known.

accepted.question_text: Is the three dimensional sphere characterized as the unique simply connected three manifold?

evidence.quote: In 1904 the French mathematician Henri Poincaré asked if the three dimensional sphere is characterized as the unique simply connected three manifold.
Perelman’s proof tells us that every three manifold is built from a set of standard pieces, each with one of eight well-understood geometries.
